_purpose: COHERENCE AUDIT — 'one question, one answer.' For each core concept the system reasons about, exactly ONE canonical accessor derives it; every other site delegates. This dimension is ORTHOGONAL to size/bloat: a codebase can score perfectly on file size, cohesion and dead code while N small, clean, single-responsibility functions independently derive the SAME concept from DIFFERENT stores and silently drift apart.
_how_to_find_answerers: Grep by STORE, not by concept name. Search for the persistence (file globs, file names, tables, registries, singletons, env vars) — every function that reads a primary store directly is a candidate answerer. Searching for the word 'roster' finds nothing useful; searching for '*.plugin' / 'roster-state.json' finds all eight.
_how_to_use: 1) Name your core concepts as QUESTIONS. 2) For each, grep the STORE to find every answerer. 3) Extract ONE canonical accessor; delegate the rest. 4) Register it below with store_patterns + an allowed map so a NEW answerer fails the build. 5) Record anything you cannot migrate yet as explicit DEBT — visible, not forgotten.

concepts.question: Which items are installed on disk?
concepts._why: Delete this example. Replace with your own concepts. In the project this guard was built for, THIS question had EIGHT independent answers reading four stores; they drifted, and the app began telling its own AI that items which plainly existed did not exist.

allowed.src/Core/ItemLibraryScanner.cs: CANONICAL — the single source of truth.
allowed.src/Loader.cs: DIFFERENT CONCEPT — enumerates ALL installed plugins (incl. non-items) for load/unload. Not the item library. Collapsing these would be premature unification.
